publication: Veenhof, K. R. (2024) Kültepe Tabletleri XII, text no. 3, TTKY VI/33c1, Ankara
genre: bare onomasticon — no verbs, commodities, or sums
consulted_via: Akkadian OCR Corpus reproduction of KT 12 transliteration and commentary
editor_description: a small list of 'Anatolian' names, many of which are unique and may have different linguistic affiliations
closed_shortcuts: watar is not a title in this text (Donbaz, Studies Veenhof p. 94 n. 56, rejected)
Nuan is not nuʾāʾum 'native Anatolian' (Donbaz NABU 1995/113, rejected)
kloekhorst_verdict: Does not recognize these as names of Anatolians; hardly any elements in common with Kanišite Hittite (2019); coincidental matches with Hittite common words (harzi 'he holds', watar 'water', haršan 'ploughed', taripia(n)zi 'they plough'); cannot be read as Hittite sentences.
distribution_note: Eleven of eleven names are unique or nearly unique in the published Old Assyrian corpus after false-positive removal. Ordinary merchant lists overlap the recurring kārum onomasticon. Captive/slave/dependent-roster is an inference from distribution, not a reading of the tablet.

names.notes: Hapax. Peruwa- head looks theophoric; the whole recurs nowhere.
Hapax. Resembles Hittite taripia(n)zi 'they plough' per Kloekhorst. Grouped by Zehnder 2010 with Pikašnurikizi and Atamakuni as Hattian or unknown, not Hittite or Luwian.
Other hits are Šarrat-Ištar names or word-boundary artifacts.
Other hits are Akkadian paḫārum 'to assemble / assembly'.
Only name with a family: Ḫarziūna (BIN 4 83; KTS 1 35a), Ḫarziga (Kt 91/k 422). Also matches Hittite harzi 'he holds'.
Hapax. Donbaz nuʾāʾum link rejected by Veenhof.
Other hits are artifacts of nēpešum spellings.
Other hits are artifacts of mu-nu-a-at spellings.

Hapax. KT 12 reads final SÍ, not the -zi of earlier secondary quotation. No internal segment recurs except possible tail -kizi ≈ independent PN Kizi, which is insufficient for a parse. Sex is inherited from Zehnder's Frauennamen catalogue, not marked on the tablet.

method_control.note: KT 12 also edits a marriage contract in which Babala is an Anatolian man's name and A-ha-a-tum looks identical to Assyrian Ahātum. Homographic traps of this kind must be flagged at attestation level; name-based sex assignment is an argument, not a datum.

next_test: Search OARE for other small tablets whose name strings return corpus counts of one — converting an unanswerable question about one name into an answerable question about a genre.
